- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 10-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative, model frequently underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
- Model tends to overpredict early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5) when sentiment is high; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., high → low → high), model misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days for smoothing.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward correction if price is above 75.00 for 3+ consecutive days.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support level, model often ignores support; add 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid false breakout.
